messages:
Anna Chen: Kicking off a short RFC/PRD thread for on-prem VPC networking. Need clear acceptance criteria, edge cases, and a proposed v1 scope. Please add must-have vs nice-to-have. Draft RFC: https://rwd.internal/rfcs/onprem-networking-draft

Raj Patel: Adding network requirements I think we should capture: BGP vs static routes, MTU handling (1500 vs jumbo), IPv6 dual-stack, NAT hairpin, IPAM integrations (Infoblox/BlueCat), route limits, and proxy/captive portal compatibility.

Maria Gomez: From product/launch POV: must-haves for launch: 1) 3 pilot customers succeed in staging, 2) security signoff, 3) KMS integration + audit logs, 4) docs + runbook, 5) SLOs defined (p95 inference over VPC <= 200ms). Decide if autoprov of subnets is in scope or deferred.

Tim O'Leary: Operational acceptance: automated networking tests (BFD/route flap), chaos tests for route loss, e2e deployment validating customer firewall rules. Rollback plan: graceful fallback to hosted endpoint with IP masking. Also need metrics for per-connection RTT and KV cache hit-rate.

Lucy Park: Security constraints: mTLS for control-plane, ability to integrate customer-managed KMS/HSM, forward audit logs to customer SIEM, and no persistent storage of customer plaintext tokens. Nice-to-have: hardware attestation and SGX.

deploy-bot: Checklist item created: "onprem-networking-rfc - network acceptance tests" -> https://rwd.internal/checklists/8245 (auto-added unit + e2e matrix).

Anna Chen: Edge cases to call out: customers behind NAT64, split DNS + private zones that overlap with our control-plane domains, asymmetric routing, MTU mismatch, captive proxies that intercept TLS. Proposed v1 scope: single VPC peering or VPN with static routes, manual IPAM mapping, IPv4 only. v2 = BGP (with MD5 auth), IPv6, IPAM sync, cross-region/custom routing. Thoughts?

Raj Patel: Agree on v1 lean scope. Note for v2: BGP MD5 and route-policy support required by some enterprises. Also need explicit tests for PMTU and ICMP-blocking networks. Example BGP snippet we should support in v2:
```
router bgp 65001
 neighbor 10.0.0.1 remote-as 65000
 neighbor 10.0.0.1 password secret-md5
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 10.10.0.0/16
```

Maria Gomez: Decision point: who manages the route table in v1? If Redwood manages routed entries we take on ops cost. Recommend customer-managed route tables for v1 to reduce ops surface.

Tim O'Leary: I'll enumerate acceptance tests to land in the RFC: 
1) Control-plane handshake uses mTLS and validates cert chains.
2) Data-plane small (1KB) and large (1MB) payload p95 <200ms in staging network.
3) Simulated rack failure: failover <5s and no request loss >1%.
4) Log forwarding to customer SIEM validated (sampled events).
5) IPAM mismatch: reject deployment with overlapping prefixes.

Anna Chen: I'll consolidate into a short PRD and owners. Quick poll for v1 scope (single VPC peering static + manual IPAM + IPv4 only): @Raj Patel @Lucy Park @Tim O'Leary — react with :thumbsup: or reply.

Raj Patel: :thumbsup:

Lucy Park: :thumbsup:

Tim O'Leary: :thumbsup:

Maria Gomez: I'll create the acceptance-criteria doc and link the RFC draft by EOD tomorrow. If anyone has additional edge cases (split TMS, industrial NATs) drop them here or ping me directly.
